pull.title: fix(install): rename every launcher shim aside, and never report a missing command as verified
pull.body:
## The defect

Installing on Windows (`irm ... | iex`) while an `mcc-claude` window and the `mcc-desktop` tray were running left **seven commands missing** and printed **"installed and verified"**.

`uv tool install --force` writes the entrypoint shims in ASCII order of the file name *including* the `.exe` suffix (`mcc-claude-old.exe` < `mcc-claude.exe`, because `-` < `.`) and **aborts the whole install on the first shim it cannot overwrite**. A running launcher holds its own `.exe`, so everything alphabetically after it was never written and uv left no `uv-receipt.toml` — `uv tool list` then reported `my-claude-code` as *malformed*.

The installer then reported success because `Invoke-RenameThenReinstall` treated that abort as "expected and harmless", set `$script:NeedDeferredFinish`, and `Configure-AndConfirmFreeClaudeCode` **skipped the command list entirely** in that state, verifying with `mcc-server --version` alone. That check can never fail: the shims are version-agnostic launchers, so an *old* shim reports the *new* version.

## Scratch reproduction — before

Scratch `UV_TOOL_DIR` / `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR`, a dummy long-lived process running from the scratch bin's `mcc-claude.exe`, then the old (no shim rename) `uv tool install --force`:

```
RUNNING dummy mcc-claude.exe pid=59656
--- uv tool install --force (OLD behaviour: no shim rename) ---
UV EXIT: 2
--- shims present after the aborted install ---
... mcc-anthropic-oauth-login.exe, mcc-chatgpt-oauth-login.exe, mcc-claude.exe, mcc-claude-old.exe
COUNT: 17 (33 expected)
MISSING: 16 -> mcc-codex.exe, mcc-commandcode.exe, mcc-compact-log.exe, mcc-crush.exe,
  mcc-desktop.exe, mcc-help.exe, mcc-init.exe, mcc-kilo.exe, mcc-kimi.exe, mcc-opencode.exe,
  mcc-opencode2.exe, mcc-pi.exe, mcc-qwen.exe, mcc-rtk.exe, mcc-server.exe, my-claude-code.exe
RECEIPT: False
error: Failed to install entrypoint
  Caused by: failed to copy file from ...\Scripts\mcc-claude.exe to ...\bin\mcc-claude.exe:
  The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
warning: Ignoring malformed tool `my-claude-code` (run `uv tool uninstall my-claude-code` to remove)
```

The cut is exactly alphabetical at `mcc-claude.exe` — `mcc-claude-old.exe` survives because `-` sorts before `.`. The user saw 7 missing rather than 16 because their pre-existing shims were only partly replaced; the mechanism is the same.

## Scratch reproduction — after

Same setup, renaming every launcher shim aside first:

```
RUNNING dummy mcc-claude.exe pid=22680
--- renaming every launcher shim aside (NEW behaviour) ---
renamed aside: 17; refused: 0
running process still alive after its own image was renamed: True
--- uv tool install --force ---
UV EXIT: 0
SHIMS PRESENT: 33
MISSING: 0
Installed 33 executables: fcc-anthropic-oauth-login, ..., my-claude-code
RECEIPT: True
--- sweep of .old-* leftovers ---
before sweep: 17
after sweep: 1 (locked ones stay: mcc-claude.exe.old-20260902-073637)
--- uv tool list ---
my-claude-code v6.30.0
```

Windows refuses to *delete* a running image but happily *renames* one, and the process keeps executing from the renamed file — the rename of the live `mcc-claude.exe` was **not** refused.

## The real installer, end to end

The published invocation is a **scriptblock** (`irm | iex`), not `-File`, so that is the form proven. Real `scripts/install.ps1` from this branch, against the scratch tool dirs only, with a dummy `mcc-claude.exe` from that scratch bin running:

```
RUNNING dummy mcc-claude.exe pid=...
shims before: 33
...
Installed 33 executables: fcc-anthropic-oauth-login, ..., my-claude-code
==> Configuring PATH and verifying My Claude Code
My Claude Code 6.30.0 is installed and verified.
New sessions and restarted servers use the new version.
Already-open windows keep running the previous version until they are
closed or restarted.
INSTALLER EXIT: 0
SHIMS AFTER: 33
LEFTOVERS: 1 -> mcc-claude.exe.old-20260902-082616
RECEIPT: True
dummy still running: True
```

And the unfixable case — a handle held with `FileShare.None`, which a normally running process does **not** do, so even `Rename-Item` is refused:

```
HARD-LOCKED mcc-kilo.exe (FileShare.None) and running mcc-claude.exe pid=...
error: Failed to install entrypoint
  Caused by: failed to copy file ... mcc-kilo.exe: ... (os error 32)
My Claude Code install failed: Command failed with exit code 2: ... uv.cmd tool install --force ...
```

Afterwards: `exe count: 33`, `receipt: True`, `old files:` (none), `old dirs:` (none) — the previous install was rolled back completely, and the failure was reported rather than dressed up as success.

## What changed

**`scripts/install.ps1`**

- `Invoke-RenameThenReinstall` renames the tool dir **and every launcher shim** aside to `<name>.exe.old-<stamp>` before `uv tool install`. New helpers `Rename-LauncherShimsAside` / `Restore-LauncherShim` / `Remove-StaleShimBackup`. The shim list is `Get-LauncherCommands`, so a neighbour tool sharing the uv bin directory is never touched (asserted).
- Post-success sweep of `*.exe.old-*` (this run's and any earlier run's); still-locked ones are skipped and reaped next install.
- On any uv failure the tool dir **and the shims** roll back, and the real error is thrown. The old "install landed, keep it and defer the one shim" branch and `$script:NeedDeferredFinish` are gone — the rename is what made that branch necessary.
- `Configure-AndConfirmFreeClaudeCode` always enumerates `Get-LauncherCommands` — one list, not two. Missing commands print `Installed, but these commands are missing: …` / `Close the mcc-claude window(s) and re-run the install command.` and `exit 1`. No "verified", no command reference.
- Deferred helper: `& $uvPath @installArgs` (was `@$installArgs`, which is *not* splatting — it collapses the array into one argument), process identity pinned by creation time as well as id (mirrors `release_updates.py:527`), and the staged wheel is swept on the failing branch too.

**The deferred helper survives**, for exactly one case: the **tool-directory** rename being refused (`Invoke-RenameThenReinstall` returns `$false`), or `uv tool dir` being unreadable. That is a genuine hard lock we cannot work around in-process. It is *not* reachable from a shim lock any more. Its wait set is still every running launcher including the tray, and that is correct now: every launcher runs its interpreter out of the tool directory, so every one of them holds the thing that is locked.

**`src/my_claude_code/application/release_updates.py`** — the dashboard/tray updater's detached helper renames the same shims aside before its uv call, sweeps them after, and reports `missing_commands` in the receipt; `ok` is now `exit code 0 AND nothing missing`. The command list comes from the installed distribution's entry points (`_published_commands`), so it cannot drift from `pyproject.toml`. `bin_dir` is taken from `server_launcher.parent` rather than a second `uv tool dir --bin`, so no uv process is spawned while the server is alive.

**`scripts/install.sh`** — reports every missing command at once instead of stopping at the first, with the same wording; `mcc-anthropic-oauth-login` added (it was published but never verified). No POSIX rename change: POSIX unlinks running files.

**Docs** — README install-troubleshooting row and a `docs/USAGE.md` §15 entry.

## Tests

New:
- `test_install_ps1_renames_every_launcher_shim_before_uv_install` — snapshots the bin directory *at the moment uv runs*; every shim must be at `*.exe.old-*`, a neighbour `ruff.exe` untouched, leftovers swept afterwards.
- `test_install_ps1_never_reports_verified_with_missing_commands` — runs the real function with the exact seven-command shape of the report; asserts non-zero exit, the message, and that `verified` never appears. Second pass with nothing missing must reach "installed and verified".
- `test_release_updates_renames_shims_before_reinstall`, `test_release_updates_receipt_lists_missing_commands`, `test_published_commands_covers_every_entry_point`.
- `test_the_windows_verification_enumerates_every_launcher_command`, `test_the_posix_verification_covers_every_native_command`, `test_the_posix_verification_reports_every_missing_command` (contract; extends the existing `Get-LauncherCommands` ↔ `pyproject.toml` guard to the verification lists).

Changed:
- `test_install_ps1_deferred_helper_invokes_uv_as_command` now asserts `& $uvPath @installArgs` and that `@$installArgs` is absent.
- `test_install_ps1_deferred_helper_runs_uv`'s stub logs **one line per argv entry** with an `ARGV-END` marker and the test asserts 8 arguments — the old `%*` stub could not tell a splat from a collapsed array.
- `test_deferred_helper_survives_native_stderr` follows `$ok` to its new definition.
- The three `Invoke-RenameThenReinstall` runtime runners dot-source the shim helpers via `_rename_functions_file`, so the real code is exercised rather than stubbed.

Removed (their premise is gone): `test_install_ps1_rename_keeps_install_when_running_shim_is_locked`, `test_install_ps1_configure_confirm_tolerates_deferred_finish`.

"Every helper called is defined" and "no `$script:` for release state" stay green; the new helpers were added to `_POWERSHELL_HELPER_NAMES`.

## Residual risks

- **A shim held with `FileShare.None`.** A normal running `.exe` is not, but a debugger, some AV products, or a handle opened deliberately can be. uv still aborts; we roll back fully and report honestly. Verified live (output above).
- **A launcher started between `Get-RunningLaunchers` and the uv call.** The no-launchers path installs directly with no rename, so that race still fails — loudly, with a real uv error, and now with honest verification behind it. Renaming unconditionally would close it; kept scoped to the reported defect.
- **`Get-ApplicationCommand` resolves through `PATH`.** If a shim exists but an identically-named command earlier on `PATH` shadows it, verification throws "resolved outside the uv tool bin directory" — pre-existing behaviour, unchanged.
- **The rollback does not remove shims uv wrote for names that did not previously exist** (a new command in the new version, when the install then fails). They are stale but harmless and are overwritten by the next install.
- PowerShell runtime installer tests **never run on Linux CI**, so a PS-only regression can still ship green there. The static guards in `tests/scripts/test_installers.py` and `tests/contracts/` run everywhere and are what CI actually enforces.

## Local verification

- `uv run --offline ruff format --check .` — 1078 files already formatted.
- `uv run --offline ruff check src/ tests/` — all checks passed.
- `uv run --offline ty check src/ tests/` — all checks passed.
- `uv run --offline pytest -q --tb=line` — see below. Baseline on this machine is **15 known failures** (6 PowerShell installer + 8 websearch + `test_catalog_publication…`); the PowerShell installer tests also flake under full parallel load and pass when rerun alone.

Version **6.30.1** (PATCH) with `uv lock` in the same commit.

commit.message:
fix(install): rename every launcher shim aside, and never report a missing command as verified

Installing on Windows while an mcc-claude window was open left seven commands
missing and printed "installed and verified".

uv writes the entrypoint shims in ASCII order of the file name *including* the
".exe" suffix -- "mcc-claude-old.exe" sorts before "mcc-claude.exe" because "-"
sorts before "." -- and aborts the whole install on the first shim it cannot
overwrite. A running launcher holds its own .exe, so every entrypoint after it
was never written and uv left no uv-receipt.toml; `uv tool list` then reported
the tool as malformed. Reproduced on a scratch UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR with a live
launcher: uv stopped at mcc-claude.exe, wrote 17 of 33 entrypoints, exited 2.

The installer then reported success because Invoke-RenameThenReinstall treated
that abort as expected and harmless, and Configure-AndConfirmFreeClaudeCode
skipped the command list entirely in that state, verifying with
`mcc-server --version` alone. That check can never fail: the shims are
version-agnostic launchers, so an old shim reports the new version.

Windows refuses to delete a running image but happily renames one, and the
process keeps executing from the renamed file. So rename the tool directory AND
every launcher shim aside before uv runs, sweep the leftovers afterwards, and
roll both back if uv fails. Measured on the same scratch setup: 17 shims
renamed, 0 refused, uv exit 0, 33 shims present, receipt written.

Verification now enumerates Get-LauncherCommands -- one list, not two, with a
contract test against pyproject.toml -- reports every missing command, and exits
non-zero without printing "verified" or the command reference. install.sh
reports every missing command the same way instead of stopping at the first.

The dashboard updater's detached helper gets the same rename-aside, sweeps the
shims it moved, and records missing_commands in its receipt.

The deferred helper survives for one case only: a refused rename of the tool
DIRECTORY, which no shim lock can reach any more. Its uv call is fixed from
`& $uvPath @$installArgs` -- not splatting; it collapses the array into a single
argument, so uv installed nothing, silently -- to `& $uvPath @installArgs`, its
wait pins each process by creation time as well as id, and it sweeps its staged
wheel on the failing branch too.

Version 6.30.0 -> 6.30.1 (PATCH).

test(install): teach the POSIX uv stub every published command, and reword a comment that tripped a message guard

The sh installer now verifies mcc-anthropic-oauth-login, which the fake uv in
tests/scripts/test_installers.py never created -- six install.sh scenarios then
failed with the (correct) new "Installed, but these commands are missing"
report. The stub now installs the full published set, fcc-* aliases included, so
it cannot fall behind the installer again.

A comment in the deferred helper contained the phrase
test_installers_allow_install_while_running_and_lead_with_mcc greps for to prove
the installer never refuses an install while the app runs. Reworded; the guard
is right to be that blunt.
